title: Preventive Maintenance
summary: Understand how planned checks can reduce surprise failures.
objectives: Distinguish preventive maintenance from corrective repair.
Connect inspections, trend review, and documentation to reliability.

vocab.def: Planned work intended to reduce the chance of failure.
Work performed to fix a problem that has occurred.
A planned check for condition or change.

sections.heading: Prevent problems when possible
sections.body: Preventive maintenance can include scheduled inspections, cable checks, monitoring-trend review, documentation review, and replacement planning.

sections.heading: Maintenance is not the same as repair
sections.body: Preventive maintenance is planned before a failure. Corrective repair responds after a problem appears. Both require the right authorization and skill.

sections.heading: Use a safe classroom plan
sections.body: Students can build a synthetic maintenance schedule or review a checklist. They should not clean energized equipment, service HVAC machinery, or handle industrial systems.

practice.prompt: Classify four synthetic tasks as preventive maintenance or corrective repair, then explain one classification.

quiz.question: Which is preventive maintenance?
options: Reviewing a monitoring trend on a planned schedule
Replacing a failed component after an outage
quiz.answer: Reviewing a monitoring trend on a planned schedule

lab.objective: Build a synthetic maintenance checklist and identify what evidence would show each check was completed.

reflectionPrompt: How can a planned check help a team communicate before a failure occurs?
